_meta.indication: Treatment of moderate to severe acute pain in adults

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study VX22-548-104 (Study 104), bunionectomy acute pain model
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, three-arm, parallel-group study with active control (HB/APAP)
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects with moderate or severe pain after a bunionectomy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: time-weighted SPID48 (sum of pain intensity difference from 0-48 hours) compared to placebo
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean difference in SPID48 of 29.3 (95% CI: 14.0, 44.6; p=0.0002) for SUZ vs placebo

nct_ctgov.title: Evaluation of Efficacy and Safety of VX-548 for Acute Pain After a Bunionectomy

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study VX22-548-105 (Study 105), abdominoplasty acute pain model
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, three-arm, parallel-group study with active control (HB/APAP)
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects with moderate or severe pain after an abdominoplasty
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: SPID48 compared to placebo
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean difference in SPID48 of 48.4 (95% CI: 33.6, 63.1; p < 0.0001) for SUZ vs placebo

nct_ctgov.title: Evaluation of Efficacy and Safety of Suzetrigine for Acute Pain After an Abdominoplasty

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (greater incidence vs placebo) were pruritus (2.1% vs 1.6% placebo), muscle spasms (1.3% vs 0.5%), increased blood creatine phosphokinase (1.1% vs 0.5%), and rash (1.1% vs 0.5%). Serious adverse events were generally consistent with known postoperative complications of surgery and their incidence was low and balanced between treatment arms.
target_moa: Selective blocker of the voltage-gated sodium channel subtype 1.8 (Nav1.8), which is predominantly expressed in peripheral sensory neurons including dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons, suppressing action potential firing and reducing pain signaling
modality: Small molecule (new molecular entity; sodium channel blocker)

advisory_committee.vote: Not presented at the Anesthetic and Analgesic Drug Products Advisory Committee because the benefit-risk assessment did not identify unexpected significant safety or efficacy issues

basis.text: Granted June 30, 2022 after phase 2 data suggesting favorable efficacy vs placebo, favorable clinical safety profile, and mechanistic rationale for less abuse potential than opioids

citations.quote: SUZ was granted Breakthrough Therapy designation after review of data from its phase 2 clinical studies suggesting favorable efficacy compared to placebo, as well as a favorable clinical safety profile and a mechanistic rationale for less abuse potential compared to opioids.
Breakthrough Therapy designation for SUZ for the treatment of moderate-to-severe acute pain was granted on June 30, 2022.

summary.text: Suzetrigine was submitted under the 505(b)(1) pathway as a new molecular entity for moderate-to-severe acute pain, with Fast Track (2020) and Breakthrough Therapy (2022) designations, and received Priority Review; it was approved via the traditional approval pathway based on two adequate and well-controlled phase 3 trials.

citations.quote: Under the 505(b)(1) regulatory pathway, Vertex Pharmaceuticals submitted new drug application (NDA) 219209, suzetrigine (SUZ) for the treatment of moderate to severe acute pain in adults.
The regulatory history is notable for Breakthrough Therapy designation and a Priority Review determination.
Fast Track designation for SUZ for the treatment of moderate-to-severe acute pain was granted on March 5, 2020.

requirement.text: 4787-7 Collect global data from prospective pregnancy exposure registry/registries, preferably disease-based multiproduct pregnancy registry/registries, using a registry-based cohort study design to compare the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to Journavx during pregnancy with unexposed comparator population(s).

citations.quote: 4787-7 Collect global data from prospective pregnancy exposure registry/registries, preferably disease-based multiproduct pregnancy registry/registries, using a registry-based cohort study design to compare the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to Journavx during pregnancy with unexposed comparator population(s). Align the U.S. study protocol with protocol(s) outside the U.S. to reach the target sample size. The registry will identify and record pregnancy complications, spontaneous abortion, stillbirths, neonatal deaths, major and minor congenital malformations, pregnancy terminations, preterm births, small-for-gestational-age births, and any other adverse outcomes, including postnatal growth and development. These outcomes should be assessed throughout pregnancy. Infant outcomes, including effects on postnatal growth and development, will be assessed through at least the first year of life.
